retained_original_metadata.title: Normal strongly continuous spatial Markov semigroups on bounded operators of separable Hilbert spaces admit weak Hudson-Parthasarathy dilations
retained_original_metadata.author: Michael Skeide
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Spatial Markov Semigroups Admit Hudson-Parthasarathy Dilations
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a noise from the spatial product system and amplifies it without changing that system. It then chooses a unitary identification carrying the original dilation isometry to the noise isometry, transports the cocycle conjugacy, and checks the conditional-expectation identity using the increasing corner projection. These compatibility steps convert product-system classification into an actual weak dilation and establish the converse through spatiality of weak dilations.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Full author Theorem2.9 proof is read and bundled. The hypotheses are point-strong continuity, normal unital CP maps on B(G), G separable, and spatiality by domination of an elementary CP semigroup as in Definition2.8. The conclusion selected is the equivalence with a weak HP dilation as in Definition2.5; weakness is essential, and the source states the converse for general HP dilations is unknown. Bhat weak dilation/product-system spatiality and Arveson cocycle classification/construction are genuinely prior background explicitly cited. The author supplies the noise amplification, compatible isometry identification, cocycle transport and corner/conditional-expectation calculation. Footnote10 provides the supporting inductive-limit explanation of infinite-dimensional complements in the nonendomorphic case. Reversible extension is contextual and not a separately counted consequence.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem2.9 first sentence: spatiality iff existence of a weak HP dilation. Reversible extension is retained as contextual source content, not an additional selected conclusion.
